analysis.title: 'Buy All The Things...' Except Oil: Buying Spree Spreads Ahead Of The Fed
key_insights: US stocks rose, credit spreads tightened and Treasury yields were flat on Oct 27, ahead of mega-cap tech earnings and the Fed decision. The dollar, gold and bitcoin also rose.
US macro data beat across durable goods orders, home sales, home prices and Conference Board consumer confidence. The US Macro Surprise Index rose to its highest since July.

WTI tested $100 as talks in Tehran (Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan officials meeting Iranian counterparts) raised hopes of de-escalation in the US-Iran conflict and eased near-term Strait of Hormuz supply fears. Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia keep a risk premium in place.

Physical oil tightness is re-emerging. Brent's December-January spread is near $5 a barrel in backwardation, up sharply from a week earlier. Crude and product inventories are almost 76 million barrels below seasonal averages.

Tanker costs remain elevated even as Middle East exports recover toward prewar levels. Iran has threatened action against Sinokor vessels, which carried almost 40% of crude exiting the Strait of Hormuz last month. Freight and insurance costs are expected to keep oil above pre-war levels.
Diesel fell to one-week lows on both sides of the Atlantic. Falling oil is helping stabilize bonds at the margin, and bond volatility is at its lowest in over a month.
10-year Treasury yields are just under 5.00%. Markets price over 90% odds that the Fed pauses at its next meeting, and odds of a December hike rose modestly back above 80%.
IG and HY credit spreads tightened, hyperscaler CDS fell to one-week lows, and data-center debt spreads compressed. The article notes some bonds still trade at 14-15% yields.

Broadcom's $63 billion AI chip financing package, arranged with Bank of America, Citigroup, Morgan Stanley and Blackstone, was completed. It closed only after Broadcom agreed to pay more and absorb losses. It lets Anthropic lease Broadcom AI chips and networking gear.
Meta completed a $25 billion equity offering about five times oversubscribed. The offering weighed on the stock but supported its credit.
AI stocks outperformed ex-AI by a wide margin (AI up 5% from Friday's close, ex-AI down 30bps), with neoclouds the biggest gainers. NDX regained its 100-day moving average and SPX topped its 50-day.

Goldman's tech desk attributed AI strength to easing AI financing concerns after the META and AVGO deals, anticipation of GOOGL, MSFT and AMZN earnings this week, and better overnight EPS (CLS +15%) with the trade bouncing from oversold conditions.

Goldman's trading floor activity was 3 out of 10, with a 1% sell skew. Long-only funds were better for sale (supply in info comms services and macro products, demand in tech and consumer discretionary). Hedge funds were 10% better to buy.
Goldman's Global Fundamental L/S exposure is at recent lows.
The dollar rose to the upper edge of its month-long range. Gold bounced back from $4,000 support and bitcoin found support at $80,000.

Bloomberg macro strategist Frank Monkam warns the next leg lower would come in three phases: rotation out of tech into defensives, contagion as credit stress spreads beyond AI, then liquidation as correlations rise and systematic deleveraging begins.

tension_points.bull_case: Successful META equity offering and AVGO financing eased AI financing concerns. Credit spreads and hyperscaler CDS tightened, AI outperformed ex-AI by about 5%, and hyperscaler earnings are anticipated this week.
tension_points.bear_case: Bloomberg's Monkam sees rotation, then contagion, then liquidation as credit stress spreads beyond AI. The AVGO deal closed only after the chip seller agreed to pay more and eat losses, and Goldman's desk saw only light dip-buying.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Credit stress reaching market breadth, which Monkam calls the critical inflection point, or an oil rebound that undermines the AI optimism.
